I have theroughly read, scratinised and en- jeyed the manuscripts “Ki Nuksa ha ka jingim ba dei ban phikir" (The Models of life to keep an eye on), written by Mr. I. Kharkongngor of Nongkrem and have found that the valuable writings unless they come in print# sooner or later, will be lost sight of in no distant fu- ture. The writer, has to the best of his ability, made a fine plausible attempt to glean facts from ancient and modern ways of social living in various phases of Khasi life. Such an attempt really needs an appreciation and encauragement from the reading public as well as from the authorities concerned, to be placed on the list of text-books of Matriculation standard, inasmuch as the language is also rich in idiomatic phrases and apt words of phraseology Dated Shillong, The 22nd September , 1964. Frank M. Pugh. By Dr. Hamlet Bareh, fa. A,, D. Phil, I have with great inteiest gone through this book “ KI NUKSA HA KA JINGIM BA DEI BAN PHIKIR*' on Khasi ethical lessons by U larington Kharkongngor. A spade work

was done during the beginning of this century to explore and present the Khasi ethical lessons and ideas by Radhou Singh Berry and Rabon Singh m their publications* They were the earliest Khasi authors who had been instrumental for bringing about the resurgence of letters in the field of Khasi literature through their works. Since then, other authors emulating them, have tried to do some- thing constructive to dig out the Khasi thoughts and ideas. But Mr. Kharkongngor has done more Justice to the subject by placing Khasi ethical thoughts and practices more systematically and coherently. The author deserves our heartiest congratulation for his laudable attempts in pre- senting aspecially this book in a very Khasi style and fashion. Following in the foot-steps of his enlightened ancestors, Mr. Kharkongngor wrote this book to inspire the present generation with good man- ners and morals. And from this book, deligent readers should acquire iustructive lessous to grow up in line with the ideal code of behaviour. This book may, therefore, be regarded as one of the best books yet published on Khasi ethics and moral lessons. And we shall expect many more contributions in this subject from other persons in the days to come. The themes which the book offers, have a special bearing particularly in the present day when so many evils have consumed the life of many young people. How many persons have wasteil their life and talents and how many have ruined them- selves because they have not received adequate moral instructions ? We should do more to bring out persons of vision and character from our society. It is my fervent wish that this book finds out its use in schools, libraries and homes. It will serve best as a supplementary Text-Book for the use of students op to secondary stage. Dated Shillong, January 6, 1966. JINGKHUNG Sl,A 1. Ka nonjjjrim nacliiii daTijjrit .... 1— 2 2. I have theroughly read, scratinised and en- 
jeyed the manuscripts “Ki Nuksa ha ka jingim 
ba dei ban phikir" (The Models of life to keep 
an eye on), written by Mr. I. Kharkongngor of 
Nongkrem and have found that the valuable 
writings unless they come in print# sooner or 
later, will be lost sight of in no distant fu- 
ture. The writer, has to the best of his 
ability, made a fine plausible attempt to glean 
facts from ancient and modern ways of social 
living in various phases of Khasi life. Such 
an attempt really needs an appreciation and 
encauragement from the reading public as 
well as from the authorities concerned, to be 
placed on the list of text-books of Matriculation 
standard, inasmuch as the language is also rich 
in idiomatic phrases and apt words of phraseology 


Dated Shillong, 

The 22nd September , 1964. 


Frank M. Pugh. 



By Dr. Hamlet Bareh, fa. A,, D. Phil, 

I have with great inteiest gone through 
this book “ KI NUKSA HA KA JINGIM BA 
DEI BAN PHIKIR*' on Khasi ethical lessons 
by U larington Kharkongngor. 

A spade work was done during the beginning 
of this century to explore and present the 
Khasi ethical lessons and ideas by Radhou Singh 
Berry and Rabon Singh m their publications* 
They were the earliest Khasi authors who had 
been instrumental for bringing about the 
resurgence of letters in the field of Khasi 
literature through their works. Since then, other 
authors emulating them, have tried to do some- 
thing constructive to dig out the Khasi thoughts 
and ideas. But Mr. Kharkongngor has done more 
Justice to the subject by placing Khasi ethical 
thoughts and practices more systematically and 
coherently. The author deserves our heartiest 
congratulation for his laudable attempts in pre- 
senting aspecially this book in a very Khasi style 
and fashion. 

Following in the foot-steps of his enlightened 
ancestors, Mr. Kharkongngor wrote this book to 
inspire the present generation with good man- 
ners and morals. And from this book, deligent 



readers should acquire iustructive lessous to grow 
up in line with the ideal code of behaviour. 
This book may, therefore, be regarded as one 
of the best books yet published on Khasi ethics 
and moral lessons. And we shall expect many 
more contributions in this subject from other 
persons in the days to come. The themes 
which the book offers, have a special bearing 
particularly in the present day when so many 
evils have consumed the life of many young 
people. How many persons have wasteil their 
life and talents and how many have ruined them- 
selves because they have not received adequate 
moral instructions ? We should do more to bring 
out persons of vision and character from our 
society. 

It is my fervent wish that this book finds 
out its use in schools, libraries and homes. 
It will serve best as a supplementary Text-Book 
for the use of students op to secondary stage. 


Dated Shillong, 
January 6, 1966.
